items.title: A Bug Just Showed XRP Could Be Minted for Free
points: A bug in the XRP Ledger's token creation mechanism allowed XRP to be minted without normal cryptographic verification, meaning new coins could theoretically be generated without legitimate authorization.
The vulnerability threatened XRP's core economic model, which relies on a fixed maximum supply of 100 billion tokens to maintain scarcity and value.
Security researchers disclosed the issue responsibly rather than exploiting it publicly, giving developers time to assess and fix the flaw before it could be exploited.
Unlimited token minting would flood the market with new supply, causing severe dilution and devaluation of existing XRP holdings.
The incident underscores the importance of rigorous code auditing in blockchain infrastructure managing billions of dollars in value.

items.title: FinCEN Withdraws Crypto Mixing Rule
points: FinCEN is withdrawing its 2023 proposal that would have labeled international crypto mixing (combining multiple users' crypto transactions to obscure their origin) a 'primary money laundering concern' under Section 311 of the Bank Secrecy Act.
The agency cited concerns the proposal's broad definition would chill legitimate privacy use, and referenced a July 2025 Presidential Working Group report recognizing lawful privacy use of mixers.
A separate 2020 proposal requiring banks to verify identities and report self-hosted wallet transactions above $3,000 is also withdrawn.
Existing obligations remain unchanged since neither proposal was finalized; FinCEN will keep monitoring mixers for illicit activity.

items.title: Stripe's Stablecoin Platform
points: Henri Stern, founder of Privy, is leading a new Stripe division to build an open, modular, global stablecoin (a cryptocurrency pegged to a stable asset like the US dollar) developer platform.

The platform integrates Bridge, Privy, Tempo, and Open USD to treat fiat and crypto as interoperable layers, letting businesses like Meta, Ramp, and Deel handle cross-border payments without rebuilding from scratch.

Stripe holds conditional OCC national bank trust charter approval in the US plus MiCA and EMI licenses in Europe, positioning it for compliance with the GENIUS Act (a US regulatory framework for stablecoins).
Existing clients show demand: Meta pays creators in real time, Ramp runs fiat and stablecoin flows in parallel, and Deel routes contractor payouts worldwide.

items.title: Polymarket Protocol V2
points: Polymarket replaced its 2019 Gnosis Conditional Tokens Framework (a smart contract system for creating conditional prediction markets) with a rebuild consolidating the stack into one ERC1155 positions contract, one pUSD collateral token, one exchange, and one router.

A new OracleAggregator with pluggable modules connects to UMA, Chainlink, and future oracle sources (services that feed real-world data to resolve market outcomes), with first-class multi-chain bridging support.
The protocol launches with four market types—Binary, Atomic Neg-risk, Incremental Neg-risk, and Combinatorial—all upgradeable behind governance.
Consolidating the stack lets the team ship new features without disrupting existing integrations.

items.title: Hack Recovery Efforts
points: Chainalysis used AI to trace the September 24 Bitget breach ($387M) to North Korean actors in under 10 minutes, compressing work that normally takes 20+ hours; funds moved across Ethereum (49.7%), XRP (40.8%), Zcash (7.6%), and Tron (1.8%) in 23 transfers within three hours.

The attacker routed stolen XRP through cross-chain liquidity protocols to convert to Bitcoin over about 36 hours, avoiding direct exchange exposure and nearing the $1 billion mark for North Korea's 2026 crypto total.

Near Intents recovered its full $3.8M in stolen funds within 48 hours after its general manager identified the attacker on-chain and issued a public return ultimatum with an implicit deanonymization threat.
The Near Intents exploit targeted a flaw in how the platform's Omni deposit/withdrawal layer interacted with its main smart contract, forcing halts across its 35-blockchain cross-chain swap service.

issues.subject: A Bug Just Showed XRP Could Be Minted for Free

headlines: A critical bug in the XRP Ledger revealed that XRP tokens could theoretically be created without cost, threatening the integrity of the token's fixed supply mechanism and raising security concerns across the network
The vulnerability exposed a fundamental flaw in the ledger's token minting process that could allow unlimited XRP generation if exploited
Security researchers identified and disclosed the issue responsibly, prompting immediate investigation and potential remediation by the XRP Ledger development community

sections.title: XRP Ledger Minting Vulnerability Details
points: 1. A bug in the XRP Ledger's token creation mechanism allowed XRP to be minted without the normal cryptographic verification requirements, meaning new coins could be generated without legitimate authorization
2. The vulnerability threatened XRP's core economic model, which relies on a fixed maximum supply of 100 billion tokens to maintain scarcity and value
3. The issue was disclosed responsibly by security researchers rather than exploited publicly, giving developers time to assess and fix the flaw before widespread knowledge could enable attacks

sections.title: Implications for XRP and Cryptocurrency Security
points: 1. The bug highlighted systemic risks in blockchain networks where flaws in consensus or token creation mechanisms could catastrophically undermine confidence in the asset
2. Unlimited token minting would flood the market with new supply, causing severe dilution and devaluation of existing XRP holdings
3. The incident underscores the importance of rigorous code auditing and security testing in mission-critical blockchain infrastructure, particularly for systems managing billions of dollars in value
